articles.title: NFL Thanksgiving Takeaways: Bears, Eagles, Bills Prevail In Day Of Instant Classics
articles.summary: NFL fans had three Thanksgiving classics to feast on. Here are our takeaways from Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills
articles.body: Three games, three Thanksgiving classics for football fans to feast on. That's how Turkey Day in the NFL went. The Bears and Lions played a thriller that ended with Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams pulling a rabbit out of his hat late, throwing the game-winning touchdown in the final seconds. Joe Milton followed that by showing off his cannon of an arm in an improbable Eagles win over the Cowboys. And to close things out, the 11th battle between Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen came down to the final play. The Bills kicked a walk-off field goal to sink the Chiefs, keeping the top spot in the AFC in a game that could determine who has home-field advantage in the postseason. We have you covered with the key takeaway from all three games. Here are the biggest things we learned from Bears-Lions, Eagles-Cowboys and Chiefs-Bills: 1.Bears-Lions Was Best Thanksgiving Game Ever? Steven Ruiz: The Lions and Bears gave us a Thanksgiving classic. You couldn’t take your eyes off the game without feeling like you were going to miss an electric play. Detroit and Chicago traded blows all afternoon. It felt like the first offense to blink would lose the game, and that’s how it ultimately played out, with the Bears prevailing. The Lions had the ball deep in Chicago territory but couldn’t convert on fourth down to seal the win. That put the ball back in Caleb Williams’ hands, and the third-year quarterback did what he’s done so often early in his career, leading a sharp two-minute drill that culminated with an inch-perfect throw to the back corner of the end zone for the game-winning score with just three seconds left on the clock. That was one of at least a dozen insane plays from the game, which also featured a 250-yard, three-touchdown performance by Jahmyr Gibbs that shouldn’t be forgotten. I’m not sure the numbers, as impressive as they are, do his performance justice. If you squinted hard enough, you might’ve thought you had been transported back to the ‘90s and were watching a prime Barry Sanders run circles around the Bears defense. But, as was so often the case during Sanders’ career, it wasn’t enough to carry Detroit to a win. Williams was just too good down the stretch. After Gibbs’ 70-yard touchdown run put Chicago in an 11-point hole early in the fourth, the Bears quarterback seemed to lock in. He connected on three straight passes, including this 41-yard strike to Rome Odunze. Maybe I’m a prisoner of the moment, but that felt like the best Thanksgiving game I’ve ever seen. We’ve had back-and-forth thrillers. We’ve had dramatic endings, like the famous Leon Lett game. We’ve had unforgettable performances, like Randy Moss’s 163-yard, three-touchdown game in Dallas. But this game had it all. It also had high stakes, with both teams entering the game 8-2 and tied atop the NFC North. Now Chicago sits alone at the top, but the Lions are right there and will have a chance to avenge this loss when the two teams meet up in Week 17. If it’s half as exciting as what we saw on Thursday, football fans will be in for a treat. 2.Joe Milton Deserves Shot As NFL Starting QB Greg Auman: Is there a bigger platform to have the best game of your career than beating the Cowboys on Thanksgiving? Eagles quarterback Joe Milton got an extra helping of holiday revenge Thursday night, throwing for 346 yards and three touchdowns to rally from a 21-point deficit and beat the team that cut him earlier this season. In one game, he had more touchdown passes than he'd totaled in his NFL career, having thrown just two in three seasons since entering the league as a Patriots sixth-round pick in 2024. This was his third start with the Eagles this season, including a win over the Steelers last week, but he'd totaled 310 yards in those two wins. With Jalen Hurts out with injury, Milton has a window ahead to show just what he's capable of as an NFL starter. He's always had a ridiculously strong arm, as could be seen Thursday in a touchdown throw to wide receiver DeVonta Smith that went 64 yards in the air. Even against a terrible Cowboys defense, Milton stepped up and led an offense that hadn't scored more than 24 points all season. The Eagles were down 31-10 with a minute left in the third quarter, and Milton was electric. He delivered two passing touchdowns and another on the ground. Then, his final drive set up Jake Elliott's 59-yard game-winning field goal with a few seconds left, completing the largest comeback in Thanksgiving NFL history. Milton can't quite cash in on the open market this spring since he's set to be a restricted free agent this offseason, which means the Eagles can tender him with a one-year offer that would at least allow them to match an offer sheet from another team. If they choose the highest tender, they could get draft-pick compensation from any team that signs him. With six games remaining, Milton would enter the offseason with a larger sample size as a starting quarterback than Malik Willis did a year ago if he started all of those games. Willis got a contract worth $67 million over three years from the Dolphins, including $45 million guaranteed. The uncertainty of Hurts' health moving forward could make the Eagles decide to pay him well enough to keep him as a starting option in 2027 as well. 3.The Bills Will Win AFC If They Have Home-Field Advantage Ralph Vacchiano: If the AFC’s road to Super Bowl LXI goes through Buffalo, the Bills will end their long drought and reach their first Super Bowl in 32 years. They may have proved that on Thanksgiving night, when they showed the entire NFL how tough it’ll be to beat them on their home turf come January. They knocked off the Kansas City Chiefs, 13-10, in a game that was played in cold, rainy and windy conditions, and on a wet and sloppy field. And over the next few months in Western New York, it’s only going to get worse. That is what these Bills (10-1) are built for. They have an explosive offense and can go point for point with anyone if that’s what they have to do. But they’re as good as any team in the NFL at grinding it out. And that’s what they did to the Chiefs. They managed just 81 passing yards from their MVP-caliber quarterback, Josh Allen, who threw two interceptions. They ran through the slop for 166 yards, though, including 117 from running back James Cook. Allen ran for 43 yards too, which was a reminder that there isn’t another team in the NFL that has a punishing, reliable 1-2 punch on the ground quite like that. They also have a powerful offensive line that just bullied the Chiefs at times. They’ve got a tough defense that never broke against Patrick Mahomes and held the Chiefs to just 241 yards. And they even have maybe the best bad-weather kicker in the game in Tyler Bass, who ignored the rain and near-30 mph winds and kicked two 50-plus-yard field goals in the fourth quarter. That included a 57-yarder as time expired to seal the wild win. That is a team built for rain, wind, snow and whatever else Western New York can offer. They want the nastiest weather they can get off Lake Erie, when nobody else will. And the Chiefs (8-3) actually might be the Bills’ biggest threat in that kind of weather. They’re kind of built the same way. They’ve got a running game better than they’ve ever had in the Andy Reid-Mahomes era, whether it’s Kenneth Walker or rookie Emmitt Johnson making it go. They’ve already proven they can grind out wins against the best of them, too. The Bills just do it better. Cook, who already has 1,177 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the season, is as punishing a running back as there is in the NFL. Allen, at 6-foot-5, 237 pounds, is the best and most powerful running quarterback in the league (and he already has 333 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns too). In nasty conditions, Allen can be impossible to drag down and Cook can be impossible to catch. And if you think that combination was hard to beat in 30-degree rain and wind on Thursday night, wait until January, when the temperatures are closer to zero and the snow starts to fall. The Bills aren't completely infallible at home. Their one loss this season was in their shiny new stadium, falling to the New England Patriots back on Oct. 4. But home-field advantage has really been the missing piece for them in their quest for the Super Bowl in the Allen era. They’ve been the No. 2 seed in the AFC four times with Allen at quarterback, but they haven’t been the No. 1 seed since 1993 — the last time they made the Super Bowl. And in the last seven seasons, in which they made the playoffs each time, they’ve been eliminated on the road five times, including three times in Kansas City. Two of those losses in K.C. were in the AFC Championship Game. They are 7-2 in Buffalo in the playoffs with Allen at quarterback, but just 1-5 on the road. So yes, home field advantage might mean more to them than anyone else. If they can get the Jaguars, Bengals, Broncos and Chiefs to come to Western New York in January, they’ll have an enormous advantage. And that should be enough to get the Bills all the way to Los Angeles on Valentine’s Day for the shot at the Super Bowl championship the entire region has been waiting a lifetime to win. articles.title: Fernando Mendoza Named Raiders Captain For Browns Game Ahead of QB's 2nd NFL Start
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza was named a team captain for their Week 12 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, the team announced Friday.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza was named a team captain for their Week 12 matchup against the Cleveland Browns, the team announced Friday.

The Raiders have named different captains for each game this season, per the team website . For Week 12, Mendoza will be accompanied by defensive end Maxx Crosby and rookie running back Dylan Laube, who was named as the special teams captain for the fourth time this season.

Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, spent most of his rookie season waiting for his opportunity behind veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. He was named the starter after the Raiders traded Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings ahead of the NFL trade deadline.

Mendoza has looked impressive in his two starts despite facing elite defensive units in both games. The 23-year-old rookie struggled to find passing yards against the Seattle Seahawks, but he played a clean and efficient game in the 21-13 loss. He found more success through the air against the Broncos, completing 18 of 37 passes for 267 yards with three touchdowns and one interception.

Mendoza will look to pick up his first win against the Browns on Sunday.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk's Status for Commanders' Game vs. Cardinals Revealed by HC Dan Quinn After NFL Return
articles.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's Washington Commanders debut will have to wait until at least Week 13.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's Washington Commanders debut will have to wait until at least Week 13.

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Friday that Aiyuk will not be activated to play in Sunday's Week 12 road game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Following his release by the San Francisco 49ers on Monday, Aiyuk signed with the Commanders' practice squad on Wednesday.

Despite Aiyuk not being ready for elevation to Washington's 53-man roster, Quinn told reporters that he is "pleased" with what he has seen out of the receiver thus far.

The 28-year-old Aiyuk has not appeared in an NFL game since October 2024, which is when he tore his ACL against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Aiyuk was expected to return and play for the 49ers at some point during the 2025 campaign, but when he stopped reporting to the team, he was placed on the reserve/left team list last December.

It wasn't until earlier this month that Aiyuk applied for reinstatement , at which point the 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption to figure out what to do with Aiyuk.

Once the exemption expired, the Niners released Aiyuk, giving him the chance to start anew in Washington.

While it has been more than two years since his last game action, Aiyuk could potentially add a dynamic element to a Washington receiving corps that is headlined by veteran Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams.

Selected 25th overall by the 49ers in the 2020 NFL draft, Aiyuk had back-to-back 1,000-yard receiving seasons in 2022 and 2023.

His best season occurred in 2023 when he caught 75 passes for a career-high 1,342 yards to go along with seven touchdowns.

In Washington, Aiyuk is reuniting with quarterback Jayden Daniels, who was his collegiate teammate for one season at Arizona State.

At 4-5-1, the Commanders trail the New York Giants by two games for the NFC East lead, but they have won back-to-back games and hold the tiebreaker over the G-Men.

Diggs, Williams, Treylon Burks (if he plays), Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey will be Daniels' options at wide receiver on Sunday, but Aiyuk could potentially be added to that mix as soon as Week 13 when the Commanders face the Tennessee Titans on the road.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Floats Potential Aaron Rodgers Landing Spot After QB's Dramatic Steelers Exit
articles.summary: Houston Rockets power forward Kevin Durant took some time on Friday to suggest the Baltimore Ravens as a landing spot for quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
Houston Rockets power forward Kevin Durant took some time on Friday to suggest the Baltimore Ravens as a landing spot for quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

Rodgers' future remains unknown after he was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday. The 42-year-old quarterback officially cleared waivers and became an unrestricted free agent on Thursday, per ESPN .

Rodgers referred to the 2026 season as his " last rodeo ," but it's unclear if he plans to sign with another team or if his last NFL snap is already behind him. Baltimore can offer something that might be appealing to the four-time NFL MVP: two games to face the Steelers, their division rival.

The Ravens have lost six consecutive games and rank last in the AFC North with a 4-7 record. They acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett ahead of the trade deadline, but the veteran has been underwhelming in his two starts with the team.

articles.title: Browns' Grant Delpit Trolls Steelers' Mike McCarthy in Video After Aaron Rodgers' Comments
articles.summary: The trolling around the Pittsburgh Steelers in the wake of Aaron Rodgers' comments about Mike McCarthy isn't slowing down.
articles.body:
The trolling around the Pittsburgh Steelers in the wake of Aaron Rodgers' comments about Mike McCarthy isn't slowing down.

Cleveland Browns safety Grant Delpit closed out his press conference on Friday by saying "1-2-3 Browns" to chuckles from the assembled media.

The comment is a reference to one of the key points Rodgers made during his Wednesday appearance on The Pat McAfee Show when he said McCarthy broke down the Steelers' halftime locker-room speech by saying "1-2-3 Packers."

At least Delpit did get the name of his team right while leaving the podium. The vibes are strong with Cleveland as it prepares to play the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday Night Football in the first game at Huntington Bank Field in this primetime spot since September 2019.

articles.title: 49ers rule out QB Brock Purdy (ankle); Mac Jones to start vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Purdy suffered the injury last week and played through it during a win over the Vikings.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers QB Brock Purdy will not play this week against the Seattle Seahawks due to an ankle injury, the team announced Friday .

Mac Jones, who won five of eight starts last season while Purdy was out with a toe injury, will start the NFC West clash Sunday.

Purdy suffered the ankle injury during last week's win over the Minnesota Vikings. The quarterback continued playing after getting hurt in the second quarter and finished with 255 passing yards and three touchdowns as the 49ers improved to 9-1.

Entering Sunday, the 49ers have a three-game lead over the Seahawks and 2 ½ over the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC West. They are currently tied with the 9-2 Chicago Bears atop the conference for the most wins.

While the 49ers will be without their starting quarterback, the Seahawks will be getting their QB1 back this week. Sam Darnold (quad) has missed the past two games, but has been cleared to return in Week 12.

Darnold needed to show Mike Macdonald that he could get through Wednesday's practice before the Seahawks head coach would be confident enough to start him. Darnold did just that and will play, though it will be behind an offensive line that will be without guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and right tackle Abe Lucas (ankle), who were ruled out earlier this week.

articles.title: Did DK Metcalf Signal to Aaron Rodgers With TD Celebration? NFL Fans Sound Off on Viral Video
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf may have sent a message to his former quarterback after scoring a touchdown in Friday's Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf may have sent a message to his former quarterback after scoring a touchdown in Friday's Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos.

Metcalf held up eight fingers after beating out Patrick Surtain II to catch a touchdown pass from Mason Rudolph in the first quarter. Fox Sports also reported he signed "stand on business."

Metcalf has previously used American Sign Language in his touchdown celebrations, including the same "standing on business" message.

His latest celebration came after the Steelers' Tuesday night announcement Rodgers would be inactive against the Broncos was followed by Rodgers criticizing the Steelers and head coach Mike McCarthy in a Wednesday appearance on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show that was followed by his release.

Some fans speculated Metcalf's celebration reflected his feelings about Rodgers' recent departure from the team.

The Steelers signed Metcalf in 2025 months before adding Rodgers, who later told McAfee the wide receiver was "a big reason I'm in Pittsburgh."

Rodgers officially cleared waivers Thursday and is now eligible to sign with any team. The Steelers (6-4) are hoping in his absence Rudolph can keep them in the running to win the AFC North, which is currently led by the Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) and Cleveland Browns (6-4).

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Steelers Top Broncos Without Rodgers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defied the expectations of many football fans on Friday by beating the Denver Broncos in the first game since cutting Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers defied the expectations of many football fans on Friday by beating the Denver Broncos in the first game since cutting Aaron Rodgers.

The Mason Rudolph-led Steelers moved to 7-4 with the 27-5 victory. That jumped them over the Cleveland Browns in the wild-card race for the moment and moved them a half-game back of the Cincinnati Bengals in the AFC North.

The pressure is now on the Bengals and Browns to win to maintain the positions they entered Week 12 in.

Denver's defeat dropped it down to the same record as the Kansas City Chiefs in the race for the AFC West.

The Buffalo Bills were the biggest beneficiary from Week 12's results in the AFC because they picked up a tiebreaker on Kansas City and opened up a two-game lead on both AFC West leaders.

Pittsburgh's stunning win moved it temporarily up to the No. 6 seed in the AFC.

Few observers believed the Steelers would be competitive with Mason Rudolph in at quarterback.

Not only were they competitive, but they controlled the Black Friday contest with the Broncos.

The Steelers are also a half-game back of the Bengals, whose Monday loss to Washington looks more consequential by the day.

Pittsburgh could finish the weekend in the No. 6 seed if the Browns fall to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday night. That game in Cleveland now carries even more importance in the AFC wild-card race. A Cleveland win more than likely drops the Raiders from the list of playoff contenders.

The flip side of Friday's result may be more meaningful to the AFC standings as a whole since Denver dropped to 8-3 and level on record with the Chiefs.

Denver and Kansas City split their regular-season series. Both teams have a 3-1 record in the AFC West. Denver is still ahead over Kansas City due to a better record in common games.

However, the divisional race is more than up for grabs now that both teams have the same record after Week 12.

The San Francisco 49ers go into Sunday with a tight edge over the Chicago Bears in the race for home-field advantage in the NFC.

The 49ers do have an injury concern at quarterback since Brock Purdy missed practice the last few days with an ankle injury.

Whether he plays or not could be a disadvantage for the 49ers against the Seattle Seahawks' tough defense.

Sunday could be an opportunity for the Seahawks to pick up a huge win in the NFC West and in the wild-card race.

The 49ers are 2.5 games clear of the Los Angeles Rams and three games ahead of the Seahawks in the NFC West.

Chicago is the biggest fan of the Seahawks on Sunday so that it can pull level on record with the 49ers.

The Bears are now in the driver's seat in the NFC North after their Thanksgiving Day win over the Detroit Lions.

articles.title: Steelers Upset Broncos Without Aaron Rodgers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Nix, DK, Rudolph, More
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to a tumultuous week by routing the Denver Broncos in their 27-5 victory on Friday.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers responded to a tumultuous week by routing the Denver Broncos in their 27-5 victory on Friday.

Mason Rudolph took over as Pittsburgh's starting quarterback after the team released four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers earlier this week, but the rest of the team stepped up to take the pressure off of the veteran backup.

The Broncos had an opportunity to take sole possession of first place in the AFC West. They entered the game as a 4.5-point favorite on FanDuel Sportsbook , but the Steelers defense had other plans. made life miserable for Broncos quarterback Bo Nix.

Here's a look at the top offensive players from both teams:

Steelers coach Mike McCarthy took a conservative approach on offense early in the game. Pittsburgh ran the ball on eight of its first 11 plays from scrimmage, including a third-and-6 on the opening drive.

Both offenses stalled out before Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt opened the scoring in the first quarter. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix fumbled the ball while facing heavy pressure, and Watt recovered it in the end zone for a touchdown.

Rudolph found wide receiver Germie Bernard on a crossing route, who turned upfield for a 58-yard gain.

Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf caught a back-shoulder throw over Broncos cornerback Patrick Surtain II to give Pittsburgh a 14-0 lead.

The Broncos offense produced minus-14 yards on nine plays over their first three possessions, but they finally managed to move the ball early in the second quarter. That drive came to a halt with Nick Herbig sacking Nix to knock Denver out of field-goal range.

Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton got his team on the board by blowing up a run and dropping Steelers running back Jaylen Warren in the end zone for a safety. Denver scored a field goal on their ensuing drive to cut the Steelers' lead to 14-5.

Pittsburgh got those three points back with Chris Boswell's 47-yard field goal, and then Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey intercepted Nix and returned it for a 36-yard touchdown.

The Broncos finished the first half with just 58 net yards on 32 offensive plays, per The Athletic's Nick Kosmider . It didn't get any better at the start of the third quarter, as Denver opened the quarter with a three-and-out.

Both teams struggled to find any rhythm offensively. Late in the third quarter, Steelers running back Rico Dowdle picked up 8 yards and 27 yards on two carries. Pittsburgh rewarded him with a third straight carry, but Dowdle fumbled the ball.

Broncos kicker Will Lutz missed a 53-yard field goal to open the fourth quarter, and Pittsburgh capitalized on the mistake. Rudolph connected with wide receiver Roman Wilson for a 37-yard gain before Pittsburgh's offense ultimately stalled, but Boswell's 33-yard field goal extended the team's lead to 22 points.

Broncos running back Jonah Coleman caught a screen and broke a couple of tackles to get into the red zone with less than 10 minutes remaining, but the drive fell apart after a false-start penalty and a sack pushed Denver backwards. Steelers' cornerback Daylen Everette intercepted Nix on a desperate fourth-and-21.

After the Kansas City Chiefs lost on Thanksgiving Day, the Broncos could have taken sole possession of first place in the AFC West with a win. Instead, the Broncos and Chiefs remain tied at 8-3.

Despite the loss, Denver remains atop the AFC West due to divisional tiebreakers. The Broncos hold the edge in common games, having defeated the Seattle Seahawks earlier this season. Kansas City lost against Seattle in Week 7.

The Steelers improved to 7-4 with the victory, moving into second place in the AFC North and pulling within a half-game of the division-leading Cincinnati Bengals. Pittsburgh currently holds the AFC's No. 6 seed, which they will have to defend against the Cleveland Browns next Sunday.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy Reacts to Mike Tomlin Calling Steelers a 'Dumpster Fire' After Aaron Rodgers Comments
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy declined to push back against former coach Mike Tomlin calling the Pittsburgh Steelers a "dumpster fire" after responding to the controversial midseason release of Aaron Rodgers by leading his team to a 27-5 Black Friday victory over the visiting Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy declined to push back against former coach Mike Tomlin calling the Pittsburgh Steelers a "dumpster fire" after responding to the controversial midseason release of Aaron Rodgers by leading his team to a 27-5 Black Friday victory over the visiting Denver Broncos.

"I really don't have one. I mean, let's just be real here," McCarthy said when asked for a response to Tomlin his postgame press conference . "There's only so much time and energy in the day, and I think you have to, when you go through things like that, I have to put all my energy into winning. And that's really what I have.

"I get that this is part of the responsibility, and the opinions and comments of others is why I'm in here to answer questions, but I'm focused on winning."

Tomlin's comments about McCarthy's team came before the Steelers' Friday win, which was highlighted by two defensive touchdowns, 142 passing yards and a touchdown from Mason Rudolph, and a mid-game message from Rodgers offering more criticism of McCarthy that was read aloud on the Prime Video broadcast by Al Michaels.

"Just very impressed, very proud of the way we handled this... The tenacity of how we played today is definitely something we can build off of," McCarthy said.

Rodgers was released by the Steelers Wednesday after he responded to the team declaring him inactive for Friday by criticizing the team and McCarthy in an appearance on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show.

McCarthy seemingly responded after Friday's win to Rodgers telling McAfee his former coach hadn't done enough to game plan or connect with the Steelers' defensive players.

"I have not spent enough time with the defense, and that's something as far as job responsibility, job description, these are things that will be looked at in the offseason," McCarthy said. "It's a point in our year where we're making adjustments, and definitely conscientious of it, but at the end of the day we have to all do our jobs and make sure we're giving the players the plan and all the other things that they need."

Rudolph said Wednesday the Steelers' leadership group had met to discuss how to move forward without Rodgers.

He then told the Amazon Prime broadcast after the win he thought "the leadership council just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy, and I think in a weird way the adversity probably brought us closer together."

McCarthy praised Rudolph as "outstanding" Friday while citing Cam Heyward and T.J. Watt as "two great examples of great leadership."

"Their energy, you could feel it, and it was needed, and those guys stepped up in a huge way... It was a special win for us. You look what happened the last two weeks. We needed a win," McCarthy said.

McCarthy signed a five-year deal with the Steelers ahead of the 2026 season. Pittsburgh Steelers president Art Rooney II told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette 's Gerry Dulac after Rodgers' appearance on ESPN he had "100 percent confidence" in McCarthy and expected him to remain in his position "this season, next season and beyond."

The Steelers will for now focus on chasing the Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) for the top of the AFC North after leapfrogging the Cleveland Browns (6-4), at least for now, by improving to 7-4 with Friday's win.

articles.title: Bo Nix Says He 'Let the Team Down' in Broncos' Upset Loss to Mike McCarthy, Steelers
articles.summary: During his postgame press conference, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix acknowledged his poor performance throughout Friday's 27-5 loss against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
During his postgame press conference , Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix acknowledged his poor performance throughout Friday's 27-5 loss against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

"It's frustrating, for sure," Nix said. "I let the team down today, and that's the last thing I want to do as the quarterback and the leader of the team."

Nix fumbled in the first quarter, which Steelers star T.J. Watt recovered in the end zone for a touchdown. The third-year quarterback said the weather affected the offense on the first few drives.

"I thought early, with the wind ... it felt like those couple of drives were the toughest," Nix said. "After that, I didn't think it was miserable to play in. [I've] played in worse. We knew it was going to be a [bad] condition game, we knew it was going to have some weather, so we just had to respond. I felt like, at times, I still threw the ball well, but obviously can't have the three turnovers."

The Broncos offense had minus-14 yards on nine plays over their first three possessions, and they didn't pick up a first down until the second quarter. Denver possessed the ball for less than two minutes on six of its drives.

Facing a 12-point deficit in the final two minutes of the first half, Nix dug his team into an even deeper hole by throwing an interception that was returned for a touchdown by Steelers cornerback Jalen Ramsey.

"I saw [Ramsey], I just didn't throw it high enough over his head," Nix said.

Denver could have taken sole possession of first place in the AFC West after the Kansas City Chiefs lost to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, but the Broncos squandered that opportunity. When asked how he expects his team to respond to this performance, Nix offered a succinct response: "Great."

Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. He was also sacked three times.

articles.title: “Our kids are so blessed, and they start at the point..”: How Russell Wilson and Ciara are teaching their kids to give back before receiving holiday gifts
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and Ciara are making sure Christmas means more than getting new toys for their children.
articles.body: Russell Wilson and Ciara are making sure Christmas means more than getting new toys for their children. The couple have a family tradition that asks their kids to give away toys before receiving fresh gifts for the holidays. And now, the lesson appears to be sticking. Their children have started suggesting ways to give back on their own, something Ciara says has been particularly sweet to see.For Wilson and Ciara, the idea goes beyond a Christmas rule. They want their children to understand how fortunate they are and why helping others should be part of their lives. With their family growing, the couple are also keeping that lesson at the center of how they celebrate the holidays.Russell Wilson and Ciara's kids are beginning to embrace the tradition themselvesThe change has been especially noticeable for Ciara. Speaking to PEOPLE recently at the Macy's Santaland premiere in New York City, she explained that the family asks their children to part with some of their toys before bringing new gifts into the house."Every year before we add new gifts, they have to subtract gifts and give it to people in need," Ciara told PEOPLE. She added that it has been particularly sweet to watch the children begin to suggest the idea themselves.Russell Wilson also spoke about the children's growing interest in giving. During the same PEOPLE interview, the retired NFL quarterback said their willingness to give back has been an "awesome blessing." For the couple, the goal appears to be making generosity something the children choose to practice, rather than something they only do when their parents ask.The family has four children: Future Zahir, 12, whom Ciara shares with rapper Future, and the couple's children Sienna Princess, 9, Win Harrison, 6, and Amora Princess, 2. Wilson and Ciara announced in September that they are expecting their fifth child. Why Russell Wilson and Ciara's giving tradition extends beyond ChristmasThe holiday lesson also reflects the work Wilson and Ciara have pursued outside their home. The couple founded the Why Not You Foundation in 2014, with a focus on education, children's health and fighting poverty.Their charitable work has also included spending time with young patients. In December 2022, Wilson and Ciara visited Children's Hospital Colorado, where they sang Christmas carols, read their children's book Why Not You? and took pictures with patients.Wilson recalled those experiences during his recent PEOPLE interview, saying the couple had enjoyed finding ways to make an impact on children and their communities. He also joked about letting Ciara handle most of the singing during those visits.But their latest family tradition puts that message into practice at home. Ciara said she wants the children to recognize how fortunate they are, especially because they have access to opportunities and comforts that she and Wilson did not have at the same age."Our kids are so blessed, and they start at the point way beyond when we started when we were their age," Ciara told PEOPLE. "So it's important to us to make sure they stay humble and understand how blessed we are."For Russell Wilson and Ciara, giving away toys before Christmas is a small step, but one they hope their children carry into adulthood. articles.title: Hailee Steinfeld shares the heartfelt story behind the song that welcomed her and Josh Allen's daughter
articles.summary: Hailee Steinfeld has revealed a special detail from the day she and Josh Allen welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen.
articles.body: Hailee Steinfeld has revealed a special detail from the day she and Josh Allen welcomed their daughter, Harper Haize Allen. The actress and Buffalo Bills quarterback became parents in April, and one song from that day has stayed with Steinfeld ever since. During an interview with Rolling Stone, the Oscar-nominated actress recalled how Allen was playing music in the delivery room when their daughter was born. The song that happened to be playing was Stevie Wonder's "Isn't She Lovely," a track that already carried a deeply personal meaning for Steinfeld.Hailee Steinfeld's daughter was born to Stevie Wonder's 'Isn't She Lovely'Hailee Steinfeld shared the story in a video posted by Rolling Stone on Instagram on November 27. She said she had prepared a birth playlist filled with songs she loved, while Allen took charge of playing the music during the delivery.The quarterback was shuffling through the playlist, with Steinfeld occasionally asking him to skip certain tracks. She recalled jokingly telling him, "She can't be born to this one."When Steinfeld later looked back at the playlist and checked the time Harper was born, she realised the song playing at that moment was "Isn't She Lovely."Wonder wrote the 1976 classic to celebrate the birth of his daughter, Aisha Morris. For Steinfeld, the song had always been beautiful, but Harper's arrival gave it a new place in her life."This song has always been so beautiful to me," Steinfeld said of the Stevie Wonder classic. " It now holds such a special place in my heart, as it was the song my daughter happened to be born to."The actress has since made the song part of Harper's everyday life. "I just love this song so much. I sing it to her all the time," Steinfeld continued. "We dance to it in the mirror. She loves it. And I hope that one day, she remembers that."Josh Allen says fatherhood has made him 'a little softer'Steinfeld has offered glimpses of motherhood through her Beau Society newsletter and social media. On her first Mother's Day in May, she shared photos of Harper holding her finger, a card featuring a tiny handprint and a breakfast spread prepared for the occasion.Allen has also spoken about the changes that came with becoming a father. During an August appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show," the Bills quarterback said having a daughter had made him "a little softer" and helped his heart grow bigger.He said he wanted to be the best dad, husband and teammate he could be, making family life part of the same ambition he brings to football.Allen's season has continued alongside those new responsibilities. The Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving, improving his record in Thanksgiving games to 4-0. Buffalo's next game is against the New England Patriots on December 6 at 4:25 p.m. ET.For Steinfeld, though, Harper's birth playlist has become more than a collection of songs. One track now connects the day her daughter arrived with a memory she hopes Harper will carry into her own life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bills Clock Operator Under Fire After Video of Controversial Chiefs Ending Surfaces
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have been on the wrong end of a few seconds against the Kansas City Chiefs before.This time, the clock might have worked in their favor.Fir...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have been on the wrong end of a few seconds against the Kansas City Chiefs before.

This time, the clock might have worked in their favor.

First-year head coach Joe Brady and the Bills improved to 10-1 with a 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, when kicker Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired. A day later, the talk has moved from Bass' leg to the Highmark Stadium game clock.

Several analysts believe Buffalo's clock operator gave the Bills extra time on Kansas City's final drive. There's also video that appears to back them up.

Bills' Clock Operator Accused of Adding Time

The Chiefs took over at their own 11-yard line with 26 seconds left in a tie game, and the Bills still had all three timeouts.

On first down, quarterback Patrick Mahomes dropped the shotgun snap and fell on it, and Buffalo called timeout. When play resumed, the clock read 25 seconds.

Sharp Football Analysis founder Warren Sharp wasn't buying it, offering video proof that something fishy happened.

"We need to talk about the clock in the final 26 seconds of the Bills-Chiefs game," Sharp posted on X. "It was reset after MULTIPLE plays to add time and NEVER was discussed. How much time? A total of 7 seconds. Just enough time after the punt to put 4 seconds on the clock & allow a game-winning Bills FG."

Sharp pointed to NBC's Mike Tirico, who told viewers that Brady was "running down to take a timeout and they get it with 19 seconds left." He said the clock got bumped up again, from 19 to 20, after running back Emmett Johnson's 5-yard run on second down.

Bills' FG Made Possible Because of Extra Time Added?

Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio counted four extra seconds . He said the clock showed 15 seconds after a third-down incompletion when it should have shown 11.

That matters. Linebacker Joe Andreessen tipped the ensuing punt. Greg Dortch returned it to the Kansas City 39-yard line with four seconds left. That was just enough for Bass to win it.

"I am at a loss for words as how this first play only took one second off the game clock," NFL analyst Ryan Paganetti posted.

Sharp also pointed out that Thursday's game should've went to overtime. He stated the extra four seconds Buffalo was seemingly given on the clock was how much time the team needed to kick its game-winning field goal.

"There is NO WAY Joe Brady called a timeout at 25 seconds," Sharp wrote . "Even with 23 seconds left, Brady no where near the ref he needed to flag down to call timeout. This is probably why you hear a whistle at 21 seconds left, because that's when Brady finally flagged the ref to call timeout.

"Possibly 21 seconds should have been on the clock, but DEFINITELY not 23 seconds, let alone 25 seconds (4 added seconds) and that's exactly what it took for the Bills to get off their final FG."

Not Everyone Is Blaming the Bills' Clock Operator

Chiefs fans were quick to take aim at whoever was running the clock in Orchard Park.

"Absolutely insane. That clock operator should be banned," one fan wrote in reply to Sharp.

"And for all the Bills fans in my mentions, the clock being adjusted correctly means this game goes to OT," another added.

However, plenty of people pointed the finger at Kansas City's own sideline instead.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid took heat for how he managed the final two possessions. Kansas City played it safe instead of pushing for a winning score.

"This game is proof Andy Reid needs to be fired," one fan proclaimed.

"Two drives in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter and the Chiefs took a combined 27 seconds off the clock and the Bills only had to use two timeouts," another pointed out.

Others noted that clock adjustments after a timeout are fairly common, and that the official clock and the broadcast clock don't always match.

Either way, the result stands. The Bills (10-1) now hold a two-game lead over the Chiefs in the race for the AFC's top seed, and the NFL hadn't publicly addressed the clock as of Friday afternoon.

articles.title: Rams offensive lineman suffered torn Achilles in 1st career start
articles.summary: Rams guard Bill Murray tore his Achilles in Wednesday's win, which was his first start in the NFL.
articles.body:
With Steve Avila still recovering from a hamstring injury, the Los Angeles Rams turned to Bill Murray at left guard on Thanksgiving Eve. It was Murray's first start in the NFL, and unfortunately, it'll be his last of the season for the Rams.

Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reported that Murray tore his Achilles in the win over the Green Bay Packers . He will miss the rest of the season, leaving the Rams without another key offensive lineman. He joins Avila, Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon as linemen who have gotten injured in the last few games.

Los Angeles has gotten dangerously thin on the offensive line, though Avila is expected to return at some point in the future, and the team did just activate Justin Dedich off injured reserve; Dedich filled in for Murray after he went down in Wednesday's game.

Murray has bounced around since going undrafted in 2020, originally signing with the Patriots. He spent four years in New England and appeared in one game before joining the Bears in 2023 and returning to the Patriots in 2025.

The Rams signed him in July and kept him on the 53-man roster.

His path to Wednesday's start makes the injury even more crushing, especially after playing well in the game. He finally earned an opportunity to start in the NFL and will now have to rehab a long-term injury in hopes of being ready for 2027. He's set to be a free agent in March.

articles.title: Metcalf Makes Wholesome Gesture in Show of Support For Former Steelers Star QB Rodgers
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is no longer with the Pittsburgh Steelers, but it appears that he is very much in the heart of wide receiver DK Metcalf. The hulking Pittsburgh...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is no longer with the Pittsburgh Steelers , but it appears that he is very much in the heart of wide receiver DK Metcalf.

The hulking Pittsburgh wideout made his presence felt late in the first quarter of Friday's game against the visiting Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh when he scored a 22-yard touchdown off a pass from Rodgers' replacement under center, Mason Rudolph. The touchdown extended Pittsburgh's lead to 14-0 following a made extra-point kick from kicker Chris Boswell.

But Metcalf turned even more heads when he seemingly showed some love to Rodgers with a series of hand gestures that translate to "Stand on business, eight," as interpreted by American Sign Language.

Here is a video of that moment in the end zone:

Metcalf Makes Wholesome Gesture in Show of Support For Former Steelers Star QB Rodgers

That was quite a statement from Metcalf amid the fallout from the bitter breakup between Pittsburgh and the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Rodgers, who might already played his last game in the league.

Many didn't feel right with the way Rodgers handled himself on the way out of Pittsburgh, but Metcalf at least appears to be in support of his now-former QB. That doesn't mean Metcalf's loyalty isn't on the Steelers. He doesn't have to pick sides, and his gesture could simply be a way of showing Rodgers that he holds no grudges against him.

Now in his second season with Pittsburgh, Metcalf entered Week 12 with 434 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 36 receptions and 74 targets.

articles.title: Bills Take Down Chiefs Despite Allen’s Struggles on Thanksgiving Day
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are always going to go as far as superstar quarterback Josh Allen takes them, but that doesn’t mean they can’t win big games without a huge...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are always going to go as far as superstar quarterback Josh Allen takes them, but that doesn't mean they can't win big games without a huge performance from him .

On Thursday , Buffalo proved that again, defeating Patrick Mahomes and the visiting Kansas City Chiefs to the tune of a 13-10 score at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park.

Allen was thankful that his teammates still made things happen that allowed Buffalo to overcome his subpar showing.

"I have to better. I need to be better. I will be better," the former NFL Most Valuable Player Allen said after the game, via John Wawrow of the Associated Press .

"Thankful for my team. Thankful for my defense. Thankful for my kicker. Thankful for James Cook and our O-linemen. This took a lot of people," he added. "I made it a little harder on ourselves. But we found a way to get (win No.) 10."

Bills Take Down Chiefs Despite Allen's Struggles on Thanksgiving Day

Allen only passed for 81 yards with zero touchdowns, while getting picked twice on 10/21 pass completions.

But Buffalo's offense got 117 rushing yards and a touchdown from James Cook III on 32 carries, while the defense held Mahomes to just 174 passing yards on 16/29 completions with zero scores.

Allen isn't always going to be at the top of his game, so it was great for Buffalo to see the other units and players stepping up and delivering the goods when the team's most important player is struggling.

Hopefully for Allen and the Bills, he'll recover his form in Week 13 against the New England Patriots on the road.

articles.title: Michael Strahan Reacts to Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Take About Pittsburgh Steelers Coach Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Strahan delivered a harsh assessment of Aaron Rodgers following the quarterback’s public criticism of Pittsburgh Steelers...
articles.body:
Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Strahan delivered a harsh assessment of Aaron Rodgers following the quarterback's public criticism of Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. The former New York Giants defensive end questioned Rodgers' decision to discuss internal team issues publicly, arguing that his comments ultimately hurt the organization.

Strahan addressed the controversy during Fox's Thanksgiving pregame coverage, joining several former players and analysts who had criticized Rodgers' appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. The quarterback had discussed his strained relationship with McCarthy after being benched, sharing several complaints about the coach's preparation and leadership.

Rodgers alleged that McCarthy arrived late to meetings and occasionally fell asleep during team sessions. He also questioned aspects of the coach's playcalling and described frustration with the team's direction. The interview attracted significant attention because Rodgers had spent years working with McCarthy during their time with the Green Bay Packers before their relationship deteriorated.

Strahan acknowledged that McCarthy might not be entirely blameless in the disagreement. However, he argued that Rodgers should have handled the situation privately instead of bringing the conflict into a public setting. The former defensive end emphasized that football remains a team sport and that players should consider how their actions affect teammates and coaches.

Michael Strahan Reacts to Aaron Rodgers' Controversial Take About Pittsburgh Steelers Coach Mike McCarthy

Strahan shared his thoughts about Rodgers amid Pittsbugh's decision to release him. This can be seen in a video shared by Fox Sports: NFL on X.

The criticism became particularly personal when Strahan addressed Rodgers' explanation that his career earnings allowed him to speak freely. The former Giants star took issue with the quarterback using his financial success to justify publicly discussing the disagreement. He argued that Rodgers' approach reflected poorly on his attitude as a teammate, regardless of whether some of his complaints about McCarthy were justified.

Pittsburgh subsequently released Rodgers following the interview, ending his time with the organization after the benching controversy. Strahan's comments reflected the broader criticism surrounding the quarterback's decision to expose internal disagreements while the Steelers were still competing. The Hall of Famer maintained that Rodgers should have protected the locker room by addressing his concerns directly with McCarthy rather than publicly criticizing the coach.

articles.title: 5 Chargers storylines ahead of Week 12 game against Patriots
articles.summary: The Chargers will look to return to the win column when they face the Patriots. Here are five key things to know ahead of Week 12.
articles.body:
The Chargers are looking to get back in the win column when they face the Patriots on Sunday.

Here are five key storylines ahead of the Week 12 matchup.

Justin Herbert (concussion) is out, so second-year DJ Uiagalelei gets the nod for his first career start. He has minimal regular-season experience. Uiagalelei finished 2-of-7 passing for 24 yards and a touchdown in relief against the Texans . Uiagalelei was given first-team reps this week, and the offense will need to simplify and lean on his strengths against a Patriots defense that has struggled recently. Jake Browning was elevated as the backup.

The Chargers' offense has found traction on the ground over the past two weeks, rushing for 318 yards, the most in the NFL across Weeks 10 and 11, with 5.0 yards per carry and 10 runs of 10-plus yards behind Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal. Meanwhile, the Patriots allowed 191 rushing yards in their last game against the Lions . Establishing the run is critical with a first-time starter under center.

The Chargers have allowed 39 sacks this season, the second-highest mark in the NFL. The line has shown signs of life the last two weeks, but a new quarterback will test that progress against New England, which ranks ninth in the NFL in sack rate (7.3%) and sixth in overall pressure rate (38.8%).

The Patriots are also starting a backup in Tommy DeVito, with Drake Maye out with a fractured fibula. The Chargers' defense has a chance to disrupt a less experienced signal-caller, but the unit has its own issues. Linebacker Daiyan Henley is out (knee), edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu is questionable (ankle), and Akheem Mesidor is doubtful. Generating pressure and forcing mistakes will be key for a defense that has given up 30.3 points per game in its last three contests.

Both teams rank near the bottom of the league in ball security, with the Patriots committing 20 giveaways and the Chargers recording 19. Forcing takeaways and relying on kicker Cameron Dicker, who has converted 10 straight field goals in November, will be vital for the Bolts to earn their first win in front of their home crowd.

articles.title: Steelers DB Jalen Ramsey honors Aaron Rodgers after win over Broncos
articles.summary: The Steelers defense stepped up against the Broncos on Friday and after the game, showed respect for former quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
On Friday afternoon, the Pittsburgh Steelers defense shut out all the noise and put on a clinic against the Denver Broncos . The Steelers defense scored two touchdowns and completely stifled the Broncos offense en route to a 27-5 victory. After a week of drama, the defense made it all about them but despite their huge performance, still understood the situation enough to give respect to Aaron Rodgers as a former teammate, regardless of how things went down.

After the game, defensive back Jalen Ramsey talked about Rodgers and showed clear respect and admiration for him and what he has meant to this team.

"It's unfortunate everything that happened, and we wish it wouldn't have gone down that way," Ramsey said. "But we're not going to act like Aaron wasn't our brother for these past two years, and a part of everything that we were doing. And he's been preparing us and getting us together. So, it's still very unfortunate, definitely. But we have got to keep rolling, and we will keep rolling. But, yeah, he's still one of us, though."

For up-to-date Steelers coverage, including any roster news and injury updates, follow us on X @TheSteelersWire and give our Facebook page a like.

articles.title: 49ers-Seahawks roundtable: How much will who's under center matter?
articles.summary: While the San Francisco 49ers will be without Brock Purdy against the Seahawks, does Seattle have a QB controversy? Plus, likely defensive standouts and what...
articles.body:
When the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Seattle to play the Seahawks seven weeks ago, it represented a big moment for both teams. The 49ers won, remaining undefeated, and have gone 4-1 since. After narrowly losing, the Seahawks have stumbled to 3-2. With Kyle Shanahan 's club riding high and leading the NFC but facing a game with Brock Purdy on the sidelines, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to these key questions going into Sunday's rematch.

First, a general NFL question: the drama in Pittsburgh. Have we seen the last of Aaron Rodgers in uniform?

Harrison Rich: It's often hard to side with Aaron Rodgers, but he seems to have the stronger argument here over Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. ESPN confirmed Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy , including sleeping in quarterback meetings and breaking down a halftime huddle by saying "1-2-3 Packers." Rodgers was waived Wednesday, but I'd imagine he plays football again in 2026 - assuming he wants to. He was still playing at a fairly high level and led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record before his ousting.

The constant in Aaron Rodgers' family and work drama: Aaron Rodgers. Given the late-career strife he's often been responsible for causing, it's notable that Rodgers' 22-season career began with him spending three good-soldier seasons sitting behind Brett Favre. Rodgers took a flamethrower to his long relationship with Mike McCarthy. It sounds as if much of what he alleged is true, but he broke an NFL code and left his playoff-contending teammates to deal with the fallout. Has he played his last snap? Not if an injury to a starting QB creates an urgent need. As former Cardinals GM Steve Keim once said of NFL teams rationalizing character concerns: "If Hannibal Lecter ran a 4.3, we'd probably diagnose it as an eating disorder."

I wouldn't be shocked if some playoff-bound team suffers an injury at quarterback and brings Rodgers in. I mean, who would be better? But, as the Black Friday broadcast team pointed out, Rodgers had already said this is his last year and has also emphasized that when he was done playing he will pull a "Keyser Soze" and disappear from public view. (Interesting to hear fellow former Cal Bear Tony Gonzalez put Rodgers on blast.) Yet there he was, airing his dirty laundry on the Pat McAfee show, blowtorching the coach he won a Super Bowl with, and texting Al Michaels during the Friday broadcast to further litigate his case. The guy desperately needs the spotlight. Pittsburgh crushed Denver, sending the message that they don't need Rodgers (though the players all still seem to like him). Rodgers' most amazing feat? Turning hapless McCarthy into a sympathetic character.

Fred Warner 's the constant for the 49ers defense, but every week turns up a new surprise hero. Last week, it was Ji'Ayir Brown. Who will it be this week?

Rich: When the Niners played the Seahawks in Week 5, multiple heroes emerged: cornerback Renardo Green, safety Malik Mustapha and defensive tackle Gracen Halton. Green picked off quarterback Sam Darnold twice and drew the primary assignment on wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had five catches for 102 yards and a touchdown. Perhaps it's not a "surprise," but it will be crucial for Green to once again win that matchup.

Branch: This wouldn't necessarily qualify as a surprise, but he would be a new 2026 defensive hero: Nick Bosa . He has zero sacks in five games (the longest in-season streak of his career had been three games), but he had five pressures in 32 pass-rushing snaps last week, numbers that would have been better if he wasn't called for a dubious roughing-the-passer penalty. Bosa is seeking his first signature play of the season. His last such play? The last time he played the Seahawks – Bosa's strip sack of Sam Darnold sealed the 49ers' 17-13 win at Seattle in the 2025 season opener.

Killion : Why not DeForest Buckner, who has a nice history against the Seahawks, with six career sacks, 23 solo tackles, 16 quarterback hits, and a fumble recovery for a touchdown?

Sam Darnold appears to be on the mend, Purdy is out, Mac Jones

will start. How much does who's under center affect your expectations?

Rich: The Seahawks have a better record in games without Sam Darnold (4-0) than they do in games with him (3-4). Is that an indicator that Seattle is a clearly better team with Drew Lock under center? Not necessarily. But it's a stat worth mentioning. As for San Francisco, there's a noteworthy drop-off from Purdy to Mac Jones , even if Jones is a starting-caliber QB in his own right. Purdy has played at an MVP level this season, while his backup hasn't taken a non-garbage time snap in a game since last season.

Branch: There's talk in Seattle that the Seahawks should stick with backup Drew Lock, who has outplayed Darnold this season while making three fill-in starts. The fact that such chatter exists reflects that the difference between the two QBs might be minimal. Meanwhile, Purdy is an NFL MVP candidate and owns the highest passer rating in league history. Jones is among the NFL's best backups, proving his worth last season while completing nearly 70% of his passes in eight starts, but the dropoff between the 49ers' top two guys isn't slight.

Who is under center is basically the most important variable in a game, particularly when one team has a quarterback who is playing like the MVP of the league but who won't be available. I love Mac Jones, his spirit, his dancing, his savvy and his sense of humor, but I've got to think the Seahawks defense is pretty fired up not to see MVP-caliber Purdy this weekend.

Do the 49ers basically sew up the NFC West, or do the Seahawks avenge their home loss?

Rich: Even without Purdy, the 49ers' offense is supremely talented and always well-prepared. All Jones needs to do is get the ball into the hands of his playmakers, and San Francisco should put up some points. The other side of the ball will determine this contest. Which version of the Niners' streaky defense shows up, and can Seattle - with a healthier and better rushing attack than it had in Week 5 - turn this into a battle of attrition? Potential rain Sunday could also make this a wackier than usual affair. 49ers 27, Seahawks 23.

Branch: Multiple readers have reached out to thank me for picking against the 49ers more than once during their 9-1 start, most recently missing the mark in Mexico City (prediction: Vikings 23, 49ers 17). It's tempting to avoid additional humiliation, but the 49ers' QB situation and the Seahawks' desperation is a combination working against the 49ers. The 49ers' only loss this season came when they were on a short week and had to travel to Atlanta. Seattle is coming off a bye and the 49ers are coming off a nine-day sojourn to Texas, Colorado and Mexico. Seahawks 27, 49ers 24.

I've been in the "let's give him some time" camp over recent years when it comes to the Bay Area anointing Purdy the MVP of the universe. Until this year. He's playing at a phenomenal level and – in my mind – has become the clear frontrunner in the NFL's MVP race. Losing him for this game is huge. It's going to be a nasty, rainy game – in other words, Seattle weather – and the Seahawks defense is not to be trifled with. Seahawks 28, 49ers 23.
